finding.claim: wipe() calls requireRole(u, "OWNER") but discards its boolean return value, so the OWNER role check never blocks the destructive repo.wipe(tenant) call. Any authenticated caller, regardless of roles, can wipe any tenant.
finding.source: wipe(User u, String tenant) handler parameters (POST /tenants/{t}/wipe per comment at src/Admin.java:24); tenant comes from the path and u from the authenticated user.

trace.note: requireRole returns boolean and does not throw

finding.guards_checked: requireRole (src/Admin.java:14-16) returns a boolean with no throw and its result is ignored at :26, so it is not an enforced control. Sibling export() (src/Admin.java:31-34) uses checkRole, which throws (:18-22), and is enforced, confirming the wipe() mismatch. No tenant-ownership check exists in either method; this is not reported because User has no tenant field and the route wiring is not in the repo (uncertain).

verdict.guard_found: requireRole (src/Admin.java:14-16) returns a boolean and never throws, and its result is discarded as a bare statement at src/Admin.java:26, so it enforces nothing. No other check sits between the caller and repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27. The working checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22) is used only by export() at :32, not by wipe().
verdict.reason: wipe() at src/Admin.java:26 discards requireRole's boolean result, so repo.wipe(tenant) at :27 runs for any caller that reaches the method, while the sibling export() at :32 uses the throwing checkRole. Every trace line matches the file. The attacker only needs to be whatever principal the route admits; the repo does not show route-level authentication or role enforcement, so that part remains unverified, but nothing in the method blocks a non-OWNER user.
